project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sharp raw compiler over all and only observationally feasible refinements, proves endpoint attainment and SCM reconstruction, and gives a total exact certifier. It proves that the bounded-window micro condition holds if and only if the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast is uniformly correct over every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model in this class; the one-lag \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) example certifies strict improvement over the label-level exclusion. It separately records that failure of the condition need not destroy identification from the full observed law. Explicit rational primal tables, pointwise dual inequalities, and an interior ledger certify relative-open strict tightening, while one multinomial event is propagated through all queries and contrasts. For response-signature compression, exact factorized push-forward fidelity, a necessary-and-sufficient factor-incidence sentence, a quotient-size bound, and the full-support parity-tilt obstruction explain precisely when unrestricted quotienting is unsound. For exact elimination, the provenance split is: direct arithmetic/degree/height/sample-point bounds; paper-owned derived bit bound. The paper-owned conversion lemma charges exact rational execution, replay traces, univariate postprocessing, algebraic comparisons, and sample-point decoding. The quotient theorem is operational rather than merely negative: it distinguishes the unrestricted-simplex lifts of RossettoAntonucci2026 and ChoeEtAl2026 from the present factorized semi-Markovian scope, gives a full-support rational rejection witness, and uses alternating-block real-algebraic elimination to decide the exact factor-incidence test before any reduced compiler is trusted.

prose_updates.related_work: Ferreira and Assaad (2026, Theorem 9) provide the summary-graph controlled-micro-direct-effect setup and an unadjusted conditional-mean identifying expression under label-level graphical conditions. In the present finite-window binary semi-Markovian class with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents, strict positive lags make \(Y_0\) terminal. The new bounded-window micro condition is exact for a deliberately narrower uniform claim: it holds if and only if \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(P_{\mathcal M})\) for every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model in this class. It removes the singleton strongly connected component requirement and the conservative exclusion of every summary bidirected edge to a summary ancestor. With \(H=L=1\), summary arrows \(B\to X\to Y\), and \(Y\leftrightarrow B\), the only \(B\to X\) placement is too late to affect controlled parent \(X_{-1}\), so the new condition holds although the label-level exclusion fails. This exactness concerns the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast, not identification from the entire observed law: with \(H=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), \(B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\to Y_0\), and \(B_{-2}\leftrightarrow Y_0\), the micro condition fails but adjustment for observed \(B_{-2}\) can still identify the effect. The present scope neither contains nor is contained in Ferreira--Assaad's broader one, because they permit contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws while this paper excludes instantaneous directed effects and imposes independent pairwise-edge-latent factorization. Duarte et al. (2024, Propositions 1--2 and Algorithm 2) provide the canonical response-function and polynomialization method adapted within each refinement; the present sharp union ranges only over refinements with a nonempty canonical fiber, and the total exact real-algebraic layer adds branchwise incompatibility certificates, endpoint isolation, causal-size bounds, and decoded SCM witnesses. Arroyo et al. (2025) are the closest fixed-graph quasi-Markovian multilinear-program comparator: their programs retain a declared ADMG, whereas the present raw product program first ranges over every positive-lag exact-summary refinement with a nonempty observational fiber, and its certification layer compares the resulting finite union exactly. Evans (2021) explains why hidden-variable DAG margins can carry constraints beyond a naive graphical or unrestricted-latent description; that perspective supports retaining the independent private and pairwise edge-factor incidence rather than replacing it by an arbitrary response-signature simplex. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025, Propositions 1--2) inform finite-window reasoning for known bounded-lag periodic ADMGs but are not the source of the positive-lag restriction. Rossetto and Antonucci (2026) and Choe et al. (2026) use unrestricted masses on response signatures or equivalence cells. Here push-forward is exact only while the induced factorized quotient family is retained: for rational \(0<\theta<1\), the full-support law \(p_\theta(w)=2^{-N}[1+\theta(-1)^{A_0\mathbin\oplus C_0}]\) belongs to an unrestricted quotient simplex, while the raw independent-edge-latent image satisfies \(F(P)=P_{00}P_{11}-P_{01}P_{10}=0\) and the displayed law has \(F(P)=\theta/4\). Thus the obstruction is not caused by zero observational cells. A finite factor-incidence sentence has an exact alternating-block real-algebraic decision procedure; after equality is established, lexicographic minimization gives a semialgebraic selector, and the derived quotient-size bound makes the guarded quotient-or-raw compiler finite. Evans (2016, Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 7.4) motivates retaining latent-margin structure. Geiger and Meek (1999) and Basu, Pollack, and Roy (1996) supply exact-elimination and complexity ancestors. The provenance split used here is: direct arithmetic/degree/height/sample-point bounds; paper-owned derived bit bound. Bellot (2024, Propositions 3--5) shows that partial graphical information can improve graph-free bounds but does not give the present temporal micro-CDE strictness region. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2020, Theorem 1) motivate whole-multinomial coverage, while Assaad, Ez-Zejjari, and Zan (2023, Proposition 7 and Theorem 1) supply the downstream direct-effect root-cause comparison made uncertainty-aware by the same-SCM tie rule.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper studies finite-window binary SCMs with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents. It excludes instantaneous directed effects and directed lags beyond \(L\), but places no \(L\)-bound on bidirected lags inside the observed \(H\)-window. Ferreira--Assaad allow contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, so the positive-lag theorem is an extension only within the present distinct scope. Its necessary-and-sufficient claim is exactly a frontier for uniform equality with the unadjusted contrast \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}\), not a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for identification from the full observed law. Indeed, with \(H=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), summary arrows \(B\to X\to Y\), and \(B\leftrightarrow Y\), a refinement containing \(B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\to Y_0\) and \(B_{-2}\leftrightarrow Y_0\) fails the micro condition, yet the observed \(B_{-2}\) supplies an alternative adjustment route under the usual positivity needed for that conditional formula. The envelope is the smallest closed interval containing all attainable CDE values; the attainable set itself need not be connected. Its nested extrema range only over refinements whose canonical feasible set is nonempty. No stationarity or infinite-history reduction is assumed. Exact certification is worst-case singly exponential in the raw response-weight dimension and is a certificate engine, not a polynomial-time method. Its provenance split is: direct arithmetic/degree/height/sample-point bounds; paper-owned derived bit bound. The derived proof explicitly charges exact rational execution, replay-trace size, square-free factorization, Sturm--subresultant isolation, algebraic sign determination and comparison, sample-point decoding, and endpoint comparison. Empty fibers receive exact branchwise infeasibility certificates, while nonempty fibers receive attained algebraic endpoints and decoded SCMs. Every graph refinement embeds in the complete temporal-order common-latent comparator, but unrestricted comparator masses are not asserted to respect missing bidirected edges. Strict tightening is relative to positive laws with a nonempty summary-graph fiber. The quotient question is resolved: factorized push-forward is exact, a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic test characterizes when the unrestricted quotient simplex is also exact, a finite quotient-size bound is proved, and a full-support rational edge-latent-chain witness shows that unrestricted quotienting fails in general. Accordingly the main compiler remains unquotiented unless the exact test certifies a particular graph. When the refinement class is a singleton the construction reduces to a fixed-graph response program.
